entities.name: Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers
entities.description: A group of life-threatening severe systemic zoonoses caused by enveloped RNA viruses from four families (Filoviridae, Bunyavirales, Arenaviridae, Flaviviridae), characterized by abrupt fever, diffuse microvascular permeability, severe thrombocytopenia, marked AST-dominant transaminitis, coagulopathy progressing to disseminated intravascular coagulation, and high mortality.

entities.name: Direct Contact with Infected Body Fluids and Nosocomial Blood Exposure
entities.description: Direct cutaneous or mucosal contact with blood, vomitus, diarrhea, saliva, amniotic fluid, or percutaneous needle-stick exposure from infected VHF patients, creating severe nosocomial transmission hazard for healthcare personnel without barrier PPE.

entities.name: Cave or Mine Exposure Harboring Rousettus aegyptiacus Fruit Bats
entities.description: Prolonged occupational or recreational exposure to subterranean caves or abandoned mines inhabited by colonies of Egyptian fruit bats (Rousettus aegyptiacus), the primary natural reservoir host of Marburg virus.

entities.name: Hyalomma Marginatum Tick Bite or Crushing Ticks
entities.description: Bite of infected Hyalomma ticks (principally Hyalomma marginatum marginatum or Hyalomma anatolicum) or direct cutaneous crushing of engorged ticks during agricultural work, transmitting Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever virus.

entities.name: Slaughterhouse Contact with Viraemic Livestock Blood or Tissues
entities.description: Occupational contact with viraemic blood, body fluids, or tissues of livestock (cattle, sheep, goats) or ostriches during animal slaughter, shearing, or butchering without barrier protection.

entities.name: Mastomys natalensis Multimammate Rat Excreta Exposure
entities.description: Ingestion of food contaminated with rodent urine/feces or inhalation of aerosolized excreta from the domestic multimammate rat (Mastomys natalensis) in endemic areas of West Africa, transmitting Lassa virus.

entities.name: Aedes and Haemagogus Mosquito Vectors
entities.description: Bites of infected Aedes (urban/peri-domestic) or Haemagogus (forest canopy) mosquitoes transmitting Yellow fever virus in tropical endemic regions of South America and sub-Saharan Africa.

entities.name: Unsafe Burial Rituals with Direct Handling of Deceased Bodies
entities.description: Traditional funeral preparation and burial practices involving direct physical contact and washing of deceased VHF patients, whose corpses maintain peak viral titers and remain intensely infectious.

entities.name: Filoviridae Family Viruses (Marburg and Ebola Viruses)
entities.description: Filamentous, enveloped negative-sense single-stranded RNA viruses (including Marburg virus, Zaire ebolavirus, and Sudan ebolavirus) causing catastrophic endothelial damage, immune cell lysis, and cytokine storm.

entities.name: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus (CCHFV)
entities.description: Enveloped tripartite negative-sense single-stranded RNA virus of the Orthonairovirus genus (Nairoviridae family, order Bunyavirales) triggering severe vascular leak, tissue factor activation, and consumptive coagulopathy.

entities.name: Lassa Virus (Arenaviridae)
entities.description: Bi-segmented ambisense single-stranded RNA virus of the Mammarenavirus genus (Arenaviridae family) endemic to West Africa, mediating severe vascular permeability, mucosal exudates, and multi-organ decompensation.

entities.name: Yellow Fever Virus (Flaviviridae)
entities.description: Positive-sense single-stranded enveloped RNA arbovirus belonging to the Flavivirus genus (Flaviviridae family) causing extensive midzonal hepatic necrosis (Councilman bodies), severe jaundice, and hemorrhagic collapse.

entities.name: Spontaneous Mucosal and Gastrointestinal Hemorrhage with Diffuse Ecchymoses
entities.description: Rapid emergence of multi-site hemorrhagic manifestations between days 3 to 7, including profuse epistaxis, bleeding gums, hematemesis ('black vomit'), melena, hematochezia, gross hematuria, and oozing from venipuncture puncture sites.

entities.name: Non-Pruritic Erythematous Maculopapular Morbilliform Rash with Centrifugal Spread
entities.description: Characteristic non-itchy erythematous maculopapular rash developing around days 5-7 on the trunk, neck, and limbs, accompanied by facial flushing and malar erythema, followed by fine post-eruptive desquamation in survivors.

entities.name: Profound Capillary Leak Syndrome with Hypovolemic Distributive Shock
entities.description: Systemic endothelial breakdown resulting in extensive vascular leakage, third-spacing, facial and periorbital edema, pulmonary edema, severe hemoconcentration, and refractory distributive/hypovolemic shock.

entities.name: Severe Exudative Pharyngitis with Retrosternal Chest Pain
entities.description: Severe tonsillopharyngeal inflammation with mucosal exudates and retrosternal chest pain present during initial febrile presentation, serving as a high-likelihood admission hallmark in Lassa fever.

entities.name: Abrupt High Fever Exceeding 39C with Excruciating Lumbosacral Myalgia and Prostration
entities.description: Explosive onset of high continuous fever (>39°C), severe chills, prostrating weakness, intense retro-orbital or frontal headache, non-purulent conjunctival injection, and incapacitating lumbar and generalized myalgia.

entities.name: Severe Rapid-Onset Thrombocytopenia Below 50,000/uL
entities.description: Precipitous reduction in admission platelet count, routinely falling below 50,000/µL and frequently below 20,000/µL in severe cases, caused by endothelial activation, platelet aggregation, and reactive hemophagocytosis.

entities.name: Biphasic Leukocyte Profile with Early Marked Leukopenia Followed by Toxic Granulation
entities.description: Initial severe leukopenia (WBC <3,000/µL) driven by absolute lymphopenia during days 1-3, shifting dramatically during clinical deterioration to neutrophilic leukocytosis with significant left shift and toxic granulation.

entities.name: Massive Transaminitis with Striking AST-Predominant Ratio Exceeding 3:1
entities.description: Marked serum aspartate aminotransferase elevation (frequently 1,000 to >10,000 U/L) disproportionately exceeding alanine aminotransferase, with an AST:ALT ratio greater than 3:1 to 5:1 reflecting extensive hepatocellular, endothelial, and lymphoid lysis.

entities.name: Consumptive Coagulopathy DIC with Marked aPTT-PT Prolongation and Severe Hypofibrinogenemia
entities.description: Severe overt disseminated intravascular coagulation manifested on admission by aPTT >60 seconds, prolonged PT/INR, marked hypofibrinogenemia (<100-110 mg/dL), and massive increases in D-dimer and fibrin degradation products.

entities.name: Polyserosal Third-Spacing on Bedside Ultrasound (POCUS)
entities.description: Point-of-care ultrasound showing prominent gallbladder wall thickening/edema, bilateral pleural effusions, ascites, and paralytic ileus secondary to acute systemic microvascular leakage, in the absence of surgical pathology.

entities.name: Complete Absence of Travel or Residence in VHF Endemic Regions Within Preceding 21 Days
entities.description: Lack of travel, residence, or direct contact with suspected/confirmed patients from known VHF endemic zones (sub-Saharan Africa, rural Anatolia, Central Asia, Balkans, South America) within the preceding 21 days reliably excludes acute VHF.

entities.name: Preserved Normal Platelet Count and Normal Coagulation Parameters in Toxic Shock
entities.description: A normal platelet count (>150,000/µL) accompanied by normal PT/INR and aPTT in a patient presenting in septic or toxic shock effectively excludes acute Viral Hemorrhagic Fever.

entities.name: Absence of Transaminitis with AST and ALT Within Normal Reference Limits
entities.description: Normal serum transaminases (AST and ALT within normal reference ranges) during an acute toxic febrile illness rules out VHF, as hepatotropic and endothelial necrosis universally causes marked transaminase elevations.

entities.name: High Peripheral Parasitemia on Giemsa-Stained Thick and Thin Blood Smears
entities.description: Presence of high-density intraerythrocytic Plasmodium falciparum ring forms responding promptly to IV artesunate without viral hemorrhagic progression or secondary transmission excludes primary VHF.

entities.name: Severe Falciparum Malaria
entities.description: Leading look-alike parasitic infection presenting with high fevers, rigors, hemolytic anemia, and splenomegaly, distinguished by high parasitemia on blood smear and response to IV artesunate.

entities.name: Severe Dengue (Dengue Shock Syndrome)
entities.description: Arboviral look-alike presenting with thrombocytopenia and plasma leakage, distinguished by timing of leak strictly at defervescence (days 3-7), transaminases rarely exceeding 1,000 U/L, and absence of human-to-human body fluid transmission.

entities.name: Leptospirosis (Weil Disease)
entities.description: Bacterial zoonotic look-alike presenting with biphasic fever, severe calf tenderness, conjunctival suffusion, direct hyperbilirubinemia, marked neutrophilic leukocytosis from day 1, and prompt response to IV penicillin or ceftriaxone.

entities.name: Fulminant Meningococcemia and Septic Shock
entities.description: Bacterial sepsis look-alike characterized by rapidly progressive purpura fulminans, markedly elevated procalcitonin (>10 ng/mL), absence of viral prodrome, and rapid microbiological response to parenteral cephalosporins.

entities.name: Early Intravenous Ribavirin in CCHF and Lassa Fever
entities.description: Early administration of intravenous or oral Ribavirin (within the first 6 days of symptom onset) demonstrates marked reduction in viral load and mortality in Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever and Lassa Fever.

entities.name: Monoclonal Antibody Cocktails for Zaire Ebolavirus (Inmazeb and Ebanga)
entities.description: Neutralizing monoclonal antibody therapeutics (Inmazeb [atoltivimab, maftivimab, odesivimab] and Ebanga [ansuvimab]) providing substantial survival benefit and viral clearance when administered early in confirmed Zaire ebolavirus.

entities.name: Total Refractoriness to Broad-Spectrum Antibacterial Therapy
entities.description: Complete lack of clinical defervescence, hemodynamic stabilization, or laboratory improvement under broad-spectrum antibacterial regimens (carbapenems, third-generation cephalosporins, vancomycin).

entities.name: Filovirus Intrinsic Resistance to Ribavirin
entities.description: Filoviruses (Ebola virus and Marburg virus) exhibit intrinsic non-responsiveness to Ribavirin therapy, showing no suppression of viremia or survival improvement.

relationships.target: Direct Contact with Infected Body Fluids and Nosocomial Blood Exposure
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, secondary human-to-human transmission, nosocomial infection, body fluids
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Catastrophic human-to-human transmission occurs via direct cutaneous or mucosal contact with blood, vomitus, diarrhea, saliva, or contaminated medical equipment, posing extreme hazard to healthcare workers.

relationships.target: Cave or Mine Exposure Harboring Rousettus aegyptiacus Fruit Bats
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, natural bat reservoir, cave exposure, filovirus
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Primary zoonotic infection of Marburg virus occurs after visiting or working in underground mines or caves colonized by Egyptian fruit bats (Rousettus aegyptiacus).

relationships.target: Hyalomma Marginatum Tick Bite or Crushing Ticks
relationships.keywords: TRANSMITTED_BY, tick vector, Hyalomma marginatum, CCHF transmission
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever virus is transmitted to humans through bites of Hyalomma marginatum marginatum ticks or direct crushing of engorged ticks during agricultural activities.

relationships.target: Slaughterhouse Contact with Viraemic Livestock Blood or Tissues
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, occupational risk, animal tissue exposure, livestock viraemia
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Occupational transmission occurs in livestock farmers, abattoir workers, and veterinarians through contact with viraemic blood and tissues of infected sheep, cattle, or ostriches during slaughtering.

relationships.target: Mastomys natalensis Multimammate Rat Excreta Exposure
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, rodent reservoir, Mastomys natalensis, Lassa virus
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmission of Lassa virus occurs through ingestion of food contaminated with rodent urine/feces or inhalation of aerosolized excreta from peri-domestic Mastomys natalensis rats in West Africa.

relationships.target: Aedes and Haemagogus Mosquito Vectors
relationships.keywords: TRANSMITTED_BY, arbovirus vector, mosquito bite, Yellow fever
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Yellow fever virus is inoculated into humans via the bites of infected Aedes aegypti (urban transmission) or canopy Haemagogus mosquitoes (sylvan forest transmission).

relationships.target: Unsafe Burial Rituals with Direct Handling of Deceased Bodies
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, funeral transmission, high viraemic corpse, contact hazard
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Direct physical contact with the body of a deceased patient during traditional funeral and washing rituals drives rapid secondary transmission due to high post-mortem tissue viraemia.

relationships.target: Filoviridae Family Viruses (Marburg and Ebola Viruses)
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, Filoviridae, Marburg virus, Ebola virus, filovirus
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by enveloped non-segmented negative-sense RNA filoviruses including Marburg virus, Zaire ebolavirus, and Sudan ebolavirus, causing massive endothelial lysis and lymphoid depletion.

relationships.target: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus (CCHFV)
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, Nairoviridae, Bunyavirales, tickborne bunyavirus
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever virus, an enveloped tripartite negative-sense RNA virus in the Orthonairovirus genus of the Nairoviridae family.

relationships.target: Lassa Virus (Arenaviridae)
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, Arenaviridae, Mammarenavirus, ambisense RNA virus
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by Lassa virus, an ambisense bi-segmented RNA virus belonging to the Mammarenavirus genus within the Arenaviridae family.

relationships.target: Yellow Fever Virus (Flaviviridae)
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, Flaviviridae, Flavivirus, arbovirus
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by Yellow fever virus, a positive-sense single-stranded enveloped RNA flavivirus producing severe midzonal hepatocellular necrosis and coagulopathy.

relationships.target: Spontaneous Mucosal and Gastrointestinal Hemorrhage with Diffuse Ecchymoses
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, hemorrhagic diathesis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] The appearance of spontaneous multisite mucosal bleeding (epistaxis, hematemesis, melena, gross hematuria) and needle-puncture ecchymoses between days 3-7 confirms decompensated hemorrhagic diathesis.

relationships.target: Non-Pruritic Erythematous Maculopapular Morbilliform Rash with Centrifugal Spread
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, cutaneous hallmark
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Emergence of a non-pruritic, erythematous maculopapular rash around day 5-7 spreading centrifugally across the trunk and neck, followed by fine desquamation, is a pathognomonic physical sign of Filovirus infection.

relationships.target: Profound Capillary Leak Syndrome with Hypovolemic Distributive Shock
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, vascular collapse
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Diffuse endothelial breakdown causing massive microvascular leakage, third-spacing, facial edema, hemoconcentration, and refractory hypovolemic/distributive shock characterizes the fatal toxic phase.

relationships.target: Severe Exudative Pharyngitis with Retrosternal Chest Pain
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, prodromal hallmark
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Marked tonsillopharyngeal exudative inflammation accompanied by severe retrosternal chest pain and facial flushing serves as a high-likelihood admission hallmark, especially prominent in Lassa fever.

relationships.target: Abrupt High Fever Exceeding 39C with Excruciating Lumbosacral Myalgia and Prostration
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, acute prodrome
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Sudden onset of high continuous fever (>39°C), conjunctival injection, severe prostration, and excruciating lumbosacral back pain and myalgias marks the acute prodrome of VHF.

relationships.target: Severe Rapid-Onset Thrombocytopenia Below 50,000/uL
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, thrombocytopenia, CBC admission hallmark, triage lab
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission CBC routinely displays profound thrombocytopenia rapidly falling below 50,000/µL and frequently below 20,000/µL during the early toxic phase, reflecting platelet consumption and reactive hemophagocytosis.

relationships.target: Biphasic Leukocyte Profile with Early Marked Leukopenia Followed by Toxic Granulation
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, leukopenia, leukocytosis with left shift, admission CBC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Triage CBC reveals an initial marked leukopenia (WBC <3,000/µL) with profound lymphopenia on days 1-3, shifting abruptly to prominent neutrophilic leukocytosis with toxic granulation as tissue necrosis progresses.

relationships.target: Massive Transaminitis with Striking AST-Predominant Ratio Exceeding 3:1
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, transaminitis, AST greater than ALT, hepatic injury
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Liver function tests demonstrate marked AST elevations (1,000 to >10,000 U/L) that dramatically exceed ALT with an AST:ALT ratio greater than 3:1 to 5:1, signaling widespread hepatocellular, endothelial, and lymphoid lysis.

relationships.target: Consumptive Coagulopathy DIC with Marked aPTT-PT Prolongation and Severe Hypofibrinogenemia
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, DIC, coagulopathy, aPTT prolongation, hypofibrinogenemia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Coagulation profile reveals profound prolongation of aPTT (>60 seconds) and PT/INR, severe hypofibrinogenemia (<100 mg/dL), and massive surges in D-dimer and fibrin degradation products.

relationships.target: Polyserosal Third-Spacing on Bedside Ultrasound (POCUS)
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, POCUS, ultrasound, polyserositis, gallbladder wall edema
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Point-of-care ultrasound demonstrates diffuse gallbladder wall thickening, ascites, and bilateral pleural effusions resulting from acute systemic capillary leakage, without bacterial focal peritonitis.

relationships.target: Complete Absence of Travel or Residence in VHF Endemic Regions Within Preceding 21 Days
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, incubation window
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Absence of travel to, residence in, or contact with cases from VHF endemic zones within the preceding 21-day maximum incubation window reliably excludes acute Viral Hemorrhagic Fever.

relationships.target: Preserved Normal Platelet Count and Normal Coagulation Parameters in Toxic Shock
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, normal platelets
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] A normal platelet count (>150,000/µL) combined with normal PT/INR and aPTT in a patient with severe prostration or shock effectively rules out acute VHF, where consumptive coagulopathy is universal.

relationships.target: Absence of Transaminitis with AST and ALT Within Normal Reference Limits
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, normal transaminases
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Normal serum transaminase levels (AST and ALT within reference ranges) during the acute toxic phase rules out VHF, as hepatic and endothelial cytolysis universally induces significant transaminitis.

relationships.target: High Peripheral Parasitemia on Giemsa-Stained Thick and Thin Blood Smears
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, malaria smear
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] High-density Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia on blood smears resolving promptly upon parenteral artesunate without coagulopathy or nosocomial transmission rules out primary VHF.

relationships.target: Severe Falciparum Malaria
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, malaria contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Severe Falciparum Malaria presents with cyclic high fevers, rigors, hemolytic anemia, and positive blood smears resolving with artesunate, whereas VHF displays AST:ALT ratios >3:1, early maculopapular rash, spontaneous mucosal bleeding, and extreme human-to-human body fluid transmission.

relationships.target: Severe Dengue (Dengue Shock Syndrome)
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, dengue contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Severe Dengue develops circulatory collapse strictly at defervescence (days 3-7) with transaminases typically below 1,000 U/L and zero human-to-human body fluid transmission, whereas VHF causes shock during ongoing high fever, massive AST elevation (>2,000-10,000 U/L), and severe nosocomial transmission risks.

relationships.target: Leptospirosis (Weil Disease)
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, leptospirosis contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leptospirosis features marked initial neutrophilic leukocytosis without early leukopenia, intense calf tenderness, conjunctival suffusion without discharge, profound direct hyperbilirubinemia, and prompt defervescence to penicillin or ceftriaxone, unlike VHF which exhibits early leukopenia, massive AST-dominant transaminitis, and complete antibiotic refractoriness.

relationships.target: Fulminant Meningococcemia and Septic Shock
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, bacterial sepsis contrast
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Meningococcemia presents with rapidly progressive purpura fulminans, markedly elevated procalcitonin (>10 ng/mL), absence of viral prodrome, and rapid response to intravenous cephalosporins, in contrast to VHF which displays viral prodromes, massive transaminitis, and refractoriness to antibacterial therapy.

relationships.target: Early Intravenous Ribavirin in CCHF and Lassa Fever
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, antiviral therapy, ribavirin, early intervention
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever and Lassa Fever show marked reductions in viremia, hemorrhagic severity, and mortality when treated within the first 6 days of symptom onset with intravenous or oral Ribavirin.

relationships.target: Monoclonal Antibody Cocktails for Zaire Ebolavirus (Inmazeb and Ebanga)
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, targeted immunotherapy, monoclonal antibodies, Ebola therapeutics
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Confirmed Zaire ebolavirus infection demonstrates significant survival benefit and rapid clearance of viremia when treated early with neutralizing monoclonal antibody cocktails (Inmazeb [atoltivimab, maftivimab, odesivimab] or Ebanga [ansuvimab]).

relationships.target: Total Refractoriness to Broad-Spectrum Antibacterial Therapy
relationships.keywords: INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO, antibiotic failure, intrinsic resistance, antibacterial refractoriness
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers exhibit absolute clinical refractoriness to broad-spectrum antibacterial regimens (carbapenems, third-generation cephalosporins, vancomycin), distinguishing viral cytolysis from bacterial sepsis.

relationships.target: Filovirus Intrinsic Resistance to Ribavirin
relationships.keywords: INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO, antiviral resistance, filovirus, Ribavirin inefficacy
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Filoviruses (Marburg virus and Ebola virus) possess intrinsic resistance to Ribavirin, demonstrating no suppression of viremia or survival improvement.
